name: Romania — Romanian parties
intro: compare it with Romanian political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Romania: those represented in the parliament (Camera Deputaților) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Camera Deputaților) after the 2024 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 331 members.

PSD.name: Partidul Social Democrat
PSD.priorities: Pensions and the elderly, Welfare state, Public services
PSD.description: Social Democratic Party, Romania's largest party, socially conservative for a European centre-left party.

USR.name: Uniunea Salvați România
USR.priorities: Fighting corruption, Rule of law, Digital innovation
USR.description: Save Romania Union, a liberal anti-corruption party popular in cities and with young voters.

Volt.name: Volt România
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

PNL.name: Partidul Național Liberal
PNL.priorities: Fiscal discipline, Competitiveness and growth, Deeper European integration
PNL.description: National Liberal Party of Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, focused on cutting Romania's large budget deficit.

UDMR.name: Uniunea Democrată Maghiară din România
UDMR.ideologies: Hungarian minority interests, Christian democracy, Pro-Europeanism
UDMR.priorities: Rights of the national minority, Regions and rural services
UDMR.description: Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania, representing the Hungarian minority and a frequent partner in government.

AUR.name: Alianța pentru Unirea Românilor
AUR.priorities: National sovereignty, Christian values, Traditional family values
AUR.description: Alliance for the Union of Romanians, a nationalist party whose leader George Simion reached the 2025 presidential run-off.

SOS.name: S.O.S. România
SOS.priorities: National sovereignty, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Christian values
SOS.description: Hard-right, pro-Russian party of Diana Iovanovici-Șoșoacă, opposed to the EU and NATO.

POT.name: Partidul Oamenilor Tineri
POT.priorities: National sovereignty, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Traditional family values
POT.description: Party of Young People, a nationalist party aligned with Călin Georgescu, whose 2024 presidential first-round win was annulled.
